messages:
Maya (AE): Heads-up — Lumen wants us to POC their "lumina-3b-q5" variant. They care about throughput, kv-cache correctness for long contexts, and a cost comparison vs f16. Can we support next-week POC?
Tom (Solutions): quick checklist request: model artifact + tokenizer vocab file + sample prompt set. Also need expected peak concurrency and whether they plan any fine-tuning during POC.
Eli (Eng-Infra): Infra note: q5 quant works but we previously saw KV cache GC pauses when seq > 5k under concurrency. We'll run a targeted KV serialization test. Need model cfg (n_layers, n_ctx, rotary dims).
Sofia (Eng-ML): ML: ask them for a small evaluation set and "gold" outputs if available. Quant profiles differ; recommend we test q5 and q8 and a float16 fallback. I can script a small bench harness.
Ken (Security): Security blockers: license audit + PII handling. If Lumen will push customer transcripts, we must enable customer-managed KMS keys and ephemeral buckets. Also need to run their vendor security questionnaire.
Nina (Product): Deployment question — do they want Hosted POC or Dedicated infra? Hosted is faster but has KMS limitations vs Dedicated. If Dedicated, we need to book GPUs (30d lead for capacity).
Sam (Acct Exec): Ballpark numbers: Hosted POC (2 wks, light traffic) estimate $1.5k-$4k. Dedicated short reserve minimum ~$20k for month. I'll draft two line items for procurement.
Maya (AE): I'll request the artifact and the prompts. Can we schedule a tech kickoff Tues 9am PT?
Eli (Eng-Infra): Tue 9am PT works. I'll prepare a verification checklist: 1) tokenization sanity check (vocab mismatch), 2) kv-cache stress (2k/5k/8k seq), 3) perf bench (batch=1,4,8), 4) fallback wiring to f16.
Sofia (Eng-ML): I'll add evaluation steps: run 100 prompts, compute avg BLEU/LL and token-level KL vs golden when provided; check output similarity threshold >= 0.9 for q5->f16 drift.
Ken (Security): I'll start the security intake and send Lumen the questionnaire link. Also request model provenance + spdx/licenses.
Tom (Solutions): ops ask for these from Lumen: model.tar.gz (weights + config), tokenizer.json, tokenizer.model if sentencepiece, sample prompts (10 short, 10 long), target p95 latency, desired SLO.
Maya (AE): Pinged Lumen — they replied: "we'll upload model bundle to the S3 link and can provide 50 example prompts (avg len 600, ~10 at 2k). We own the model license (MIT-like)."
Sofia (Eng-ML): Good. once bundle's up I'll run local scan with `redwoodctl model scan` and then a smoke run: ```redwoodctl serve-bench --model ./lumina.tar --profile q5 --batch 8 --seq 600```
Eli (Eng-Infra): Example KV test command I'll run: ```python infra/kv_stress.py --model ./lumina.tar --seq 5000 --concurrency 6 --runs 100```
Sam (Acct Exec): noted on license = MIT-like. Drafting Hosted + Dedicated pricing stubs, will post to thread.
Ken (Security): MIT-like helps but still need third-party weight provenance. Keep me looped. If they insist on SSO/audit we recommend Dedicated.
Nina (Product): Product note — document the POC report with a short table: q5 perf, q8 perf, f16 perf; kv-cache integrity pass/fail at seq thresholds; delta in output quality. This helps sales and procurement.
Tom (Solutions): Once I get model scan output I'll post a short summary: tokenizer OK? config OK? any missing fields?
RedwoodBot: Ticket created: POC-4827 (lumina-3b-q5 onboarding), assignee: Tom (Solutions).
Maya (AE): Thanks team. I'll collect the bundle and invite everyone to Tue 9am PT. Please add any pre-kickoff checks here. :pray:
